data.hypothesis: A conservative sparse-work gate can route very sparse cases to obstacle inclusion-exclusion while preserving the fast two-row segmented NEON scan for denser cases, improving sparse workloads without giving up the dense-path gains.
data.notes: Combines the declared sparse inclusion-exclusion approach with the AArch64 segmented scan and its portable scalar fallback. No commands or local measurements were run; the controller should evaluate the complete program.
transformations: Store blocked columns in sorted, deduplicated per-row lists and use two rolling rows for the dense path.
Select factorial-based binomial inclusion-exclusion for sparse obstacles when estimated pair work is at most one 1024th of dense grid work; handle blocked endpoints and N=1 explicitly.
Use the AArch64 four-lane segmented prefix scan, unrolled over two groups, with scalar handling for remaining columns and non-AArch64 targets.
